Method of Attack: Malware disguised as chat apps (mobile remote access trojan - MRAT) installed via social engineering using fake profiles and fake apps to bait Israeli soldiers
Malware installed on mobile phones to collect phone number, GPS info, storage data, SMS messages, take pictures, steal contact list, download and execute files
Communication with command and control (C2) server over MQTT protocol
Discoverer: Israel Security Agency (ISA, a.k.a. Shin Bet)
Impacted Systems: Mobile phones of Israeli soldiers in the Israel Defense Forces (IDF)
Attack Vector: Social engineering via fake female personas on messaging platforms (Facebook, WhatsApp, Telegram, Instagram)
Victims instructed to download fake chat apps from provided links (not from official app stores)
